audience: Codex operators and Decodex Control Plane builders
text: Codex MultiAgentV2 renamed its trigger-turn tool: `assign_task` is now `followup_task`. PR #25636 keeps legacy rollout-trace classification for `assign_task`, so old traces still reduce correctly. Source: https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/25636
evidence_notes: PR #25636 source evidence confirms the v2 exposed tool name changed from assign_task to followup_task.
The upstream impact artifact classifies the change as a Decodex compatibility risk with an operator_impact Publisher angle.
The 2026-06-04 Asia/Shanghai cap day had zero checked-in published @decodexspace social_post/v1 records before this run.
Chrome loaded X while signed in as Yvette Carlisle @hackink when viewing @decodexspace, so target-account verification for @decodexspace did not pass.
A bounded account-switcher probe did not expose @decodexspace as the active posting account and instead navigated to the @hackink profile.
Chrome tabs opened for account-check/readback were finalized with no kept handoff tabs.

claims.text: Codex MultiAgentV2 renamed the trigger-turn tool from assign_task to followup_task.
Legacy rollout traces still classify assign_task as an agent-task dispatch.

decision.reason: Source-backed MultiAgentV2 rename affects operator expectations and Decodex compatibility planning, but this run failed closed because Chrome was not verified as logged in to @decodexspace.

failure.details: Chrome page readback showed the active X session as Yvette Carlisle @hackink while viewing @decodexspace. The workflow requires Chrome to be logged in as @decodexspace before composing, and a bounded switcher probe did not produce reliable @decodexspace posting identity evidence. Duplicate detection, compose, media upload, and final URL readback were therefore not attempted.

caveats: No media was generated or uploaded because the run failed before compose.
Retry publication only after Chrome/X visibly verifies @decodexspace as the active posting account.
